    Storm Damage Roof Checklist for Hunter Valley Property Owners

    Strong wind, hail, falling branches and heavy rain can damage roofs quickly. The first step is to protect people and avoid creating a second hazard while checking what happened.

    Request a Free QuoteBack to Blog
    HomeBlogStorm Damage Roof Checklist for Hunter Valley Property Owners

    Table of contents

    1. 1.Put safety before inspection
    2. 2.Visible signs to record
    3. 3.What a roof make-safe is designed to do
    4. 4.Planning permanent storm repairs
    5. 5.Frequently asked questions

    Put safety before inspection

    Stay away from fallen powerlines, sagging ceilings, loose roof materials and areas where water is near electrical fittings. Do not climb onto a wet or storm-damaged roof.

    • Keep children and pets away from debris
    • Move valuables only when safe
    • Photograph damage from ground level
    • Call emergency services for immediate life-safety hazards

    Visible signs to record

    From a safe location, look for missing tiles, lifted metal sheets, damaged ridge caps, bent gutters, fallen branches, debris in valleys and water entering ceilings or walls.

    Note the time of the storm, the rooms affected and whether the leak continues after the rain eases.

    What a roof make-safe is designed to do

    A make-safe is temporary work intended to reduce immediate risk or weather exposure. Permanent repairs may require separate materials, better weather or a more detailed assessment.

    Planning permanent storm repairs

    Once the roof is safe, the damaged components can be assessed and a permanent scope prepared. This may include tiles, sheets, flashings, gutters, roof penetrations or structural elements affected by impact.

    Frequently asked questions

    What is the difference between a make-safe and a permanent repair?+
    A make-safe reduces immediate risk or water entry. Permanent work restores the damaged roof components properly.
    Should I keep photos of the damage?+
    Yes. Ground-level photos, dates and notes can help explain the event and the areas affected.
    Can hail damage a metal roof without creating an immediate leak?+
    Yes. Some impacts affect coatings, profiles or fixings and may need closer assessment even when no leak is visible.
